messages.subject: Reparameterizing truncated distributions
parts:
Hi,

I have a, hopefully, simple question about reparameterizing random coefficients.

If a hierarchical model includes random coefficients from a truncated distribution, is it still possible to employ the Matt Trick? I think the truncation prevents it from being appropriate but would be great to get confirmation.  

parameters {  
  real<lower=0> alpha[R];  
  real alpha_mu;  
  real alpha_sigma<lower=0>;  
...  
}  
model {  
  for (r in 1:R){  
   alpha[r] ~ normal(alpha_mu,alpha_sigma)T[0,];  
  }  
... 
}


Thanks,
Dominic

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Reparameterizing truncated distributions
parts:
If you take:

alpha <- alpha_raw * sigma_alpha + mu_alpha

and you need alpha > 0, this translates to:

alpha_raw * sigma_alpha + mu_alpha > 0

and hence

alpha_raw > - mu_alpha / sigma_alpha

So you'd need to have this rather messy specification::

parameters {
real<lower=(- mu_alpha / sigma_alpha)> alpha_raw;
...
transformed parameters {
real<lower=0> alpha;
alpha <- alpha_raw * sigma_alpha + mu_alpha;
...
model {
alpha_raw ~ normal(0,1) T[(- mu_alpha / sigma_alpha), ];
...

The combination of the lower bound on alpha_raw and truncation on
normal means it's not going to have the nice normal(0,1)
property, but I don't have a good sense of how it'll behave
on the unconstrained scale geometrically or what the efficiency of
the truncation with a parameter as argument is going to be like.

- Bob
